hints: Notice the charge is $+2.0 \text{ mC} = 2.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ C}$ and the upward electric force is $1.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ N}$.
Recall that electric field strength is force per unit charge, $E = F/q$, with unit $\text{V m}^{-1}$ equivalent to $\text{N C}^{-1}$.
Compare the direction of the force on a positive charge with the field direction, and check whether you divided $F$ by $q$ or $q$ by $F$.
walkthrough: Identify the given values: $q = +2.0 \text{ mC} = +2.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ C}$ and $F = 1.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ N}$ upwards in a vertical uniform field.
State the governing relation for field strength: $E = F/q$.
Substitute with units: $E = (1.0 \times 10^{-2} \text{ N})/(2.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ C}) = 5.0 \text{ N C}^{-1} = 5.0 \text{ V m}^{-1}$.
Determine direction: electric force on a positive charge is in the same direction as the electric field, so an upward force means the field is upwards.
The combination $5.0 \text{ V m}^{-1}$ upwards matches one option. This is option D.

options.A: Inverts the ratio as $q/F$ to get $0.20$ and reverses the direction; force on a positive charge is along the field, not opposite.
options.B: Uses $q/F$ instead of $F/q$, giving $0.20 \text{ V m}^{-1}$; the magnitude calculation is upside down.
options.C: Gives the correct magnitude of $5.0 \text{ V m}^{-1}$ but the wrong direction; an upward force on a $+2.0 \text{ mC}$ charge needs an upward field.
options.D: $E = F/q = 5.0 \text{ V m}^{-1}$ and the field points upwards, same direction as the force on the positive charge.
